headline: Dataset redundancy and label leakage distort evaluation of protein and gene embeddings
label: Embedding Benchmark Validity
summary: Embedding-based annotation and classification benchmarks are being re-examined for label circularity, anisotropy, and non-redundant test sets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether reported performance of biological sequence and text embeddings survives controls for label construction and sequence redundancy. GO-derived NCBI and Alliance gene summaries leak evaluation labels into gene-text embedding benchmarks, inflating AUROC, and the authors introduce GeneProv for matched evaluation. In protein language model benchmarking, 12 embeddings are compared against MMseqs2 and Foldseek for remote-homology retrieval, and severe anisotropy is reported to substantially impair retrieval. A separate XGBoost study on trigram and physicochemical features separates CARD resistance genes at AUROC 0.982 but fails on ResFinder sequences non-redundant with the training data, pointing to cross-database redundancy as a driver of apparent accuracy. What is new is the explicit diagnosis of these failure modes rather than aggregate benchmark gains.
